text:
elaine-iam: heads up — SCIM provisioning failing for AcmeCorp after their IdP swap. Symptoms: user creates 500, role duplicates, and provisioning service logs KMS decrypt errors. P1 until we have a fix.

sam-sre: on it. can you paste the provisioning error log?

elaine-iam: pasted: 
```
2026-03-18T21:07:16Z scim-provisioner PUT /Users/0ab12 500 "encrypt/decrypt error"
error: kms:Decrypt failed for ciphertext blob; keyId="alias/redwood-prod"; AwsErrorCode=InvalidCiphertextException
trace_id=evt-9f3a
```

matt-security: if KMS returned InvalidCiphertextException it's usually the key changed or the ciphertext was re-encrypted with a different CMK. did we rotate the alias last night?

deploy-bot: deploy job #4572: key-rotation-runner completed at 2026-03-18T02:12:01Z. Changed alias/redwood-prod -> arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-rotated.

anya-devex: quick thought — SCIM payload includes externalId and group mappings. If externalId or claim mapping changed during the IdP swap we could be sending new IDs which cause the provisioning engine to attempt decryption of older metadata. Also duplicates could come from group case-sensitivity mismatch.

sam-sre: can someone grab a failing SCIM request body? need to see if encrypted metadata is present (we wrap some fields).

elaine-iam: sample (redacted): 
```
{ "id": "0ab12", "userName": "jane@acme.com", "externalId": "acme|12345", "meta": { "encrypted_blob": "CiD...==" } }
```

matt-security: that encrypted_blob was produced with the old CMK. If the alias now points at a new key but the ciphertext still references the old key material, KMS will fail. Two options: 1) re-point alias back to previous key until we re-encrypt, 2) re-encrypt blobs with new key.

oncall: impact: all new SCIM requests for that customer fail (500). Other customers unaffected. No elevated CPU or token leak. Marked P1 and paged KeyMgmt team.

sam-sre: checking audit logs for alias swap: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=alias/redwood-prod --start-time 2026-03-17T00:00:00Z
```
found: Principal=ops-keymgr changed targetKeyId at 2026-03-18T02:11:58Z.

matt-security: was that an authorized rotation? who approved? need approval id in ticket. Also check KMS key policy — if the new key lacks decrypt permissions for our provisioner role that could also surface similarly.

anya-devex: while you do that, quick remediation suggestion: add a transient fallback that, if KMS.Decrypt fails with InvalidCiphertextException, the provisioner will skip re-encrypt and enqueue user to a re-encryption queue (so we don't block). low-risk short-term.

elaine-iam: small additional note — RBAC duplicates: we have duplicate group records created because the IdP sent group name as "Engineering" and "engineering" for different SAML assertions. that created two role entries in our RBAC and SCIM attempted to reconcile both which pulled different ciphertexts.

sam-sre: running a small dedupe against staging to validate SQL: 
```
BEGIN;
DELETE FROM rbac_roles r1 USING rbac_roles r2
WHERE r1.id > r2.id AND lower(r1.name) = lower(r2.name) AND r1.org_id = r2.org_id;
COMMIT;
```
Do not run on prod without approvals.

matt-security: confirmed alias swap was manual by ops-keymgr; approval ticket #KM-782 exists but doesn't reference SCIM. I'll escalate. Also checking key policy now.

deploy-bot: audit entry: audit:event id=evt-9f3a actor=ops-keymgr action=UpdateAlias target=alias/redwood-prod oldKey=key/efgh previousPasswordVersion=20260123 newKey=key/abcd-rotated

matt-security: key policy includes provisioner role decrypt on new key. So permission likely OK. I suspect ciphertext was generated with the old CMK which is now scheduled for deletion or isn't accessible. Need to check if old key still enabled.

sam-sre: AWS KMS console shows key/efgh status: 'PendingDeletion' scheduled 2026-04-30. But it's still enabled today. hmm. But alias moved so kms can't locate matching material for that ciphertext? Need to run KMS API decrypt with ciphertext and specify key id?

elaine-iam: can we quickly re-encrypt the few failing customers' blobs using a one-off tool that calls KMS:Decrypt with the old key ARN and then KMS:Encrypt with the new key, update DB? small script should do it.

matt-security: I can run that after we validate it's allowed. We must log re-encryption and add audit entry. I'll prepare script stub.

matt-security: script sketch: 
```
for row in SELECT id, encrypted_blob FROM provisioning_queue WHERE customer_id = 'acme' AND status='failed'; do
  plaintext=$(aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/efgh)
  newblob=$(aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/redwood-prod --plaintext "$plaintext")
  UPDATE provisioning_queue SET encrypted_blob=$newblob, status='queued' WHERE id=$row.id;
done
```

anya-devex: if we do that, also fix the SCIM mapping for externalId normalization and add a quick job to canonicalize group names to lowercase to prevent duplicates.

oncall: agreed. next steps: 1) matt to draft re-encrypt plan + audit log, 2) sam to temporary fallback enqueue on InvalidCiphertextException, 3) ops-keymgr to confirm approval scope (KM-782), 4) operations to run dedupe plan and canonicalize groups.

elaine-iam: I'm creating an incident: INC-2026-03018-scim-kms. Adding links to audit and the sample payloads.

matt-security: assigning to me for re-encryption and postmortem. will update incident with timeline and root cause.

sam-sre: pushing hotfix for fallback queue now, will cut a canary deploy to provisioning-staging in 10m.

idp-bot: SAML metadata refresh event: acme-idp refreshed keys 2026-03-18T01:55:12Z — flagged by idp-sync.

elaine-iam: thanks all. will keep monitoring and notify AcmeCorp support. :white_check_mark:

oncall: incident severity P1, paged oncall and keymgr. next update in 30m or earlier on changes.
